easy.def: To touch lightly with something soft.
examples: She dabbed her eyes.
Dab the paint.
I dabbed the cut.

more.def: To touch something lightly and quickly with something soft, or to put on a small amount.
examples: She dabbed her eyes with a tissue.
Dab a little paint on the corner of the picture.
I dabbed the cut with a clean cloth.

easy.def: A small amount.
examples: A dab of paint.
Put a dab on it.
A dab of butter.

more.def: A small amount of something soft or wet.
examples: She put a dab of paint on her nose.
I added a dab of butter to the potatoes.
A dab of glue held the paper in place.

easy.def: To try something just a little.
examples: I dabble in painting.
He dabbled in music.
She dabbles with clay.

more.def: To take part in something in a light way, without being serious about it.
examples: He dabbled in music but never took lessons.
I like to dabble in painting on weekends.
Ducks dabble their bills in the water.

easy.def: A small dog with a long body and short legs.
examples: A dachshund ran.
The dachshund has short legs.
We have a dachshund.

more.def: A small dog with a long body, short legs and long ears.
examples: The dachshund trotted down the path.
A dachshund has a long back and short legs.
Our dachshund barks at the mail carrier.

easy.def: A word for your father.
examples: My dad cooks dinner.
Dad drove me to school.
I hugged my dad.

more.def: A word used for a father, in everyday talk.
examples: My dad taught me how to ride a bike.
Her dad is a bus driver in our town.
Dad, can you help me with my model plane?

easy.def: A name for your father.
examples: My daddy reads me stories.
Daddy took us to the park.
I hugged my daddy.

more.def: A word that young children use for their father.
examples: The little boy ran to the door and shouted, "Daddy's home!"
Her daddy taught her how to ride a bike.
My daddy and I baked pancakes on Sunday.

easy.def: A yellow spring flower shaped like a trumpet.
examples: The daffodil is yellow.
I picked a daffodil.
A daffodil blooms in spring.

more.def: A yellow spring flower with a trumpet-shaped center.
examples: The daffodil bloomed in early spring.
A bunch of daffodils sat in the vase.
Daffodils grow from bulbs.

easy.def: Happening every day.
examples: We have daily chores.
She takes a daily walk.
The paper is a daily paper.

more.def: Done or happening each day.
examples: We take a daily walk after dinner.
The daily paper comes at seven.
A daily chore is feeding the dog.

easy.def: In a small, careful and pretty way.
examples: The girl daintily held her cup.
The cat daintily stepped.
He daintily held the cup.

more.def: In a delicate and careful way.
examples: She daintily sipped her tea.
The cat daintily stepped over the puddle.
He daintily folded the napkin.

easy.def: Small, light and pretty.
examples: The cup is dainty.
She took dainty steps.
A dainty bird landed.

more.def: Small, delicate and pretty.
examples: She took dainty steps across the stage.
A dainty tea cup sat on the tray.
The dainty bird landed lightly on the branch.

easy.def: A place that makes milk foods, like cheese and butter.
examples: We visited a dairy.
The dairy has cows.
Milk comes from the dairy.

more.def: A farm or business that makes milk and foods from milk, such as cheese, butter and yogurt.
examples: We took a trip to a dairy to watch the cows being milked.
The dairy delivers milk and butter to the stores in town.
Cheese and yogurt are called dairy foods.

easy.def: A raised stage in a room.
examples: The teacher stood on the dais.
The dais was high.
She sat on the dais.

more.def: A raised platform at the front of a hall, where speakers or important people stand or sit.
examples: The principal stood on the dais to give a speech.
The throne sat on a dais.
The winners stepped up onto the dais.

easy.def: A small white flower with a yellow middle.
examples: I picked a daisy.
Daisies grow in the grass.
She put a daisy in her hair.

more.def: A small flower with many thin white petals around a yellow center, which grows wild on lawns and in fields.
examples: Daisies spread across the meadow in spring.
He made a chain out of daisies.
A bee landed on the daisy and sipped nectar.

easy.def: A valley.
examples: We walked in the dale.
The dale is green.
Sheep live in the dale.

more.def: A valley, especially in the north of England.
examples: Sheep grazed in the green dale.
A stream ran through the dale.
We hiked through the dale.

easy.def: A white dog with black spots.
examples: A dalmatian has spots.
The dalmatian is white.
We saw a dalmatian.

more.def: A large white dog with black spots.
examples: A dalmatian rode on the fire truck.
The dalmatian has black spots all over its coat.
Our neighbor has a friendly dalmatian.

easy.def: A wall that holds back water.
examples: The dam stops the river.
Beavers build a dam.
The dam is strong.

more.def: A wall built across a river to hold back water.
examples: Beavers built a dam across the stream.
The dam holds back the river.
The dam makes a big lake.

easy.def: To hurt or break something.
examples: Rain can damage a book.
Do not damage the plants.
The dog damaged my shoe.

more.def: To harm something so that it is broken or works less well.
examples: The storm damaged the roof of the barn.
Too much sun can damage your skin.
Hail damaged the cars parked on the street.

easy.def: A little bit wet.
examples: The grass is damp.
My towel is damp.
The air felt damp.

more.def: Slightly wet, but not dripping.
examples: The grass was damp with morning dew.
Wipe the table with a damp cloth.
The cave was cool and damp inside.

easy.def: To make a little wet.
examples: Dampen the cloth.
The rain dampened our picnic.
She dampened the stamp.

more.def: To make a little wet, or to make something less lively.
examples: Dampen the cloth before you wipe the table.
The rain dampened our spirits.
She dampened the stamp with water.

easy.def: Something that makes things less lively.
examples: Rain put a damper on the picnic.
The news was a damper.
The damper ruined the fun.

more.def: Something that spoils the fun, or a plate in a chimney that controls the fire.
examples: Rain put a damper on our picnic.
The sad news was a damper on the party.
He closed the damper to slow the fire.

easy.def: A young woman in old stories.
examples: The knight helped a damsel.
A damsel waited in the tower.
The damsel was kind.

more.def: An old word for a young woman, used in stories about knights.
examples: The knight rescued a damsel in the old tale.
A damsel looked from the castle tower.
In the story, a damsel gave the knight a flower.

easy.def: To move your body to music.
examples: We dance at parties.
She danced to the song.
The kids danced in the rain.

more.def: To move your body in time to music.
examples: The class learned to dance for the school show.
Bees dance to tell other bees where the flowers are.
They danced in the kitchen while the cookies baked.

easy.def: Steps that you do to music.
examples: I learned a new dance.
We did a silly dance.
The dance was fun to watch.

more.def: A set of steps and movements done to music.
examples: The class practiced a folk dance for the school show.
Her dance told a story without any words.
The honeybee does a special dance to show where flowers are.

easy.def: A person who dances.
examples: The dancer twirled.
She is a dancer.
The dancers wore red.

more.def: A person who dances, especially as a job or a hobby.
examples: The dancer twirled across the stage.
The dancers practiced a new routine.
My sister is a ballet dancer.

easy.def: A yellow weed that turns into a fluffy ball.
examples: I blew a dandelion.
The dandelion is yellow.
A dandelion grew in the grass.

more.def: A common plant with a yellow flower that becomes a ball of white fluff.
examples: I blew the fluffy seeds off a dandelion.
A dandelion grew in a crack in the sidewalk.
Dandelions are weeds, but their flowers are bright.

easy.def: Very good.
examples: That is a dandy idea!
We had a dandy time.
What a dandy hat!

more.def: Very good or fine; first-rate.
examples: That is a dandy idea for the school fair!
We had a dandy time at the lake last summer.
Grandpa wore a dandy new hat to the picnic.

easy.def: A chance that something bad may happen.
examples: The sign warns of danger.
The kitten was in danger.
There is danger near the river.

more.def: A chance that someone could be hurt.
examples: The sign warned of danger on the thin ice.
The lost kitten was in danger.
Firefighters face danger every day.

easy.def: Not safe.
examples: It is dangerous to play near the road.
A hot stove is dangerous.
That dog is not dangerous.

more.def: Likely to cause harm or injury.
examples: Swimming in the river is dangerous when the water is high.
It is dangerous to ride a bike without a helmet.
Some wild mushrooms are dangerous to eat.

easy.def: In a way that could cause harm.
examples: The car drove dangerously.
The ice was dangerously thin.
He leaned dangerously.

more.def: In a way that is likely to cause harm.
examples: The car drove dangerously close to the curb.
The truck swerved dangerously close to the wall.
He leaned dangerously over the edge.

easy.def: To hang and swing loosely.
examples: My feet dangle from the chair.
The keys dangled.
A spider dangles from a thread.

more.def: To hang loosely so that something swings back and forth, or to hold something so that it hangs and swings.
examples: She sat on the dock and let her feet dangle in the cool water.
A spider dangled from the ceiling on a silky thread.
He dangled a toy mouse above the kitten.

easy.def: Cold and wet in a yucky way.
examples: The cave was dank.
The cellar is dank.
A dank room.

more.def: Unpleasantly damp and cold.
examples: The dank cellar smelled of mold.
We shivered in the dank cave.
A dank mist hung over the swamp.

easy.def: Marked with small spots of light or color.
examples: The horse has a dappled coat.
Sun fell in dappled light.
A dappled deer.

more.def: Marked with small, rounded spots or patches of light, shade or color.
examples: Sunlight came through the leaves and made dappled light on the path.
The dappled deer was almost invisible among the trees.
The horse had a gray dappled coat.

easy.def: To ask someone to do something brave.
examples: I dare you to jump!
She dared him to climb.
They dared me to touch it.

more.def: To challenge someone to do something brave or risky.
examples: My brother dared me to jump off the diving board.
She dared her friend to eat a hot pepper.
They dared each other to cross the creek.

easy.def: To be brave enough to try.
examples: I would not dare to climb that high.
He did not dare look.
She dared to ask a question.

more.def: To be brave enough to try something that is scary or hard.
examples: No one dared enter the dark cave.
She dared to speak up in front of the class.
I would not dare touch a sleeping bear.

easy.def: A person who does risky things.
examples: The daredevil did a jump.
A daredevil climbed.
The daredevil was brave.

more.def: A person who is bold and likes to do dangerous things.
examples: The daredevil jumped his bike over a ramp.
A daredevil walked on a rope high above the crowd.
The daredevil wore a helmet for his show.

easy.def: Brave and willing to take chances.
examples: The daring boy climbed the tree.
It was a daring jump.
She is daring.

more.def: Brave and willing to take risks or try new things.
examples: The daring boy climbed to the top of the tallest tree.
She made a daring jump across the stream.
The daring explorer crossed the deep canyon on a rope bridge.

easy.def: With little or no light.
examples: It is dark at night.
The room is dark.
Turn on the light; it is dark.

more.def: With little or no light, so that it is hard to see.
examples: The cave was dark, so we used flashlights.
It gets dark early in the winter.
A dark cloud covered the sun.

easy.def: Close to black.
examples: She has dark hair.
He wore a dark coat.
The dark soil is wet.

more.def: Deep in color, close to black.
examples: She wore a dark blue coat.
The dark soil is good for plants.
His dark hair curled at the ends.

easy.def: To make darker.
examples: The sky will darken.
Clouds darkened the day.
The room darkened.

more.def: To become or make something darker.
examples: The sky began to darken before the storm.
Clouds darkened the afternoon.
She darkened the drawing with a pencil.

easy.def: Made darker.
examples: The darkened room was quiet.
The darkened sky.
The darkened street was empty.

more.def: Made dark or dim.
examples: We tiptoed down the darkened hall.
We walked through the darkened street.
A darkened sky warned of the storm.

easy.def: In a scary, unhappy way.
examples: He looked darkly at the sky.
The old house loomed darkly.
She spoke darkly.

more.def: In a gloomy, scary or unfriendly way.
examples: The storm clouds gathered darkly over the hills.
He frowned darkly and said nothing.
The old castle stood darkly against the sky.

easy.def: No light.
examples: The room was in darkness.
We sat in the darkness.
The darkness is scary.

more.def: The lack of light, or the dark.
examples: The room was filled with darkness.
We walked through the darkness with a flashlight.
A candle lit up the darkness.

easy.def: A name you call someone you love.
examples: Come here, darling.
Goodnight, darling.
Thank you, darling.

more.def: A word used to speak lovingly to someone.
examples: Grandma said, "Come here, darling, and give me a hug."
It is time for bed, darling.
Thank you, darling; that was kind of you.

easy.def: Sweet and nice to look at.
examples: What a darling puppy!
She wore a darling hat.
The baby has a darling smile.

more.def: Very sweet and charming.
examples: The kitten looked darling in its tiny sweater.
What a darling little cottage with a flower garden!
The twins wore darling matching hats.

easy.def: A mild word for being upset.
examples: Darn, I forgot my hat!
Oh darn!
Darn, it is raining.

more.def: A mild word that people say when they are a little upset or annoyed.
examples: Darn, I missed the bus!
Oh darn, the lid is stuck.
Darn, I left my book at home.

easy.def: To move quickly and suddenly.
examples: The fish darted away.
A bird darted by.
She darted across the road.

more.def: To move quickly and suddenly in one direction.
examples: The little fish darted between the rocks.
A squirrel darted up the tree.
She darted out of the room to answer the phone.

easy.def: A small pointed stick that you throw at a target.
examples: He threw a dart.
The dart hit the board.
A dart is small.

more.def: A small, thin, pointed object that is thrown at a target in a game or shot from a toy.
examples: He threw a dart at the board and hit the bullseye.
The toy gun shoots a foam dart.
A tranquilizer dart helped the vet calm the animal safely.

easy.def: To run fast for a short way.
examples: I dash to the door.
The boy dashed across the road.
She dashed for the bus.

more.def: To run quickly for a short distance.
examples: I dashed to the door when the bell rang.
The squirrel dashed up the tree.
The rabbit dashed into its hole.

easy.def: A short race or a short line.
examples: He won the dash.
The dash is a short line.
The runner won the hundred-yard dash.

more.def: A short, fast run, or a short horizontal mark that is used in writing.
examples: He won the hundred-yard dash.
Add a dash between the two words.
We made a dash for the car in the rain.

easy.def: The panel in front of the driver of a car.
examples: The dashboard has lights.
The dashboard shows the speed.
Dad looked at the dashboard.

more.def: The panel in front of the driver that has the dials and controls of a vehicle.
examples: The dashboard showed that the car was low on gas.
A toy dog sat on the dashboard.
Dad looked at the dashboard to check the speed.

easy.def: Looking bold, smart and full of style.
examples: The prince looked dashing.
A dashing hat.
He wore a dashing coat.

more.def: Having a bold, lively and stylish look.
examples: The prince looked dashing in his red coat and tall boots.
She wore a dashing hat with a long feather.
The dashing pirate captain waved to the crowd.

easy.def: Cruel and sneaky.
examples: The dastardly villain.
A dastardly plan.
He was dastardly.

more.def: Cruel, sneaky and mean, like a villain in an old story.
examples: The dastardly villain tied the hero to the tracks in the old movie.
He had a dastardly plan to steal the pies.
The dastardly fox tricked the hens.

easy.def: Facts and numbers that you collect.
examples: We collected data about the weather.
The data shows that it rained.
The class kept data on plants.

more.def: Facts and numbers that are collected to study something.
examples: Scientists collect data to learn about the weather.
We wrote the data in a table.
The data showed that most students walk to school.

easy.def: The day of the month and year.
examples: What is the date?
Write the date.
Today's date is May 5.

more.def: The day, month, and year when something happens.
examples: Please write the date at the top of your paper.
What is the date of the school play?
His birthday is a date I never forget.

easy.def: A sweet, sticky brown fruit.
examples: I ate a date.
Dates grow on palm trees.
She likes dates.

more.def: A sweet, sticky brown fruit with a long seed that grows on palm trees.
examples: Dates grow on tall palm trees in hot places.
She put a chopped date in the muffin batter.
A date is a sweet snack that is full of energy.

easy.def: To spread something sticky or wet roughly.
examples: She daubed paint.
He daubed mud on the wall.
The child daubed the paper.

more.def: To spread wet material such as paint or mud on a surface in a rough way.
examples: The child daubed paint all over the paper.
They daubed mud on the walls of the hut.
He daubed glue on the paper.

easy.def: A girl who is someone's child.
examples: My mom is Grandpa's daughter.
She has a son and a daughter.
The farmer's daughter fed the hens.

more.def: A girl or woman, when you are talking about her parents.
examples: The farmer's daughter fed the chickens every morning.
Their daughter was born in the spring.
Aunt Jo's daughters are my cousins.

easy.def: To make someone feel scared or not sure.
examples: The tall wall daunted her.
The big hill did not daunt us.
He was daunted by the test.

more.def: To make someone feel nervous or less brave about doing something.
examples: The steep hill did not daunt the young hikers.
The long list of jobs daunted him at first.
She was daunted by the huge crowd but sang anyway.

easy.def: Scary because it looks too hard.
examples: The big hill looks daunting.
The test is daunting.
Climbing was a daunting task.

more.def: Making you feel nervous or unsure because it seems very hard.
examples: The tall mountain looked daunting to the new climbers.
Learning a new language can be a daunting task.
The huge pile of dishes was daunting.

easy.def: To move slowly and waste time.
examples: Do not dawdle.
He dawdled on the way.
She dawdled over her food.

more.def: To waste time by moving slowly.
examples: Don't dawdle, or we'll miss the bus.
He dawdled on the way home from school.
She dawdled over her breakfast.

easy.def: The time when the sun comes up.
examples: The birds sing at dawn.
We woke at dawn.
The sky turns pink at dawn.

more.def: The first light of the day, just as the sun starts to rise.
examples: Farmers get up at dawn to milk the cows.
The campers watched the dawn color the lake gold.
At dawn the whole forest filled with the sound of birds.

easy.def: The time from morning to night.
examples: We played all day.
It was a sunny day.
What a fun day!

more.def: The time when it is light outside, or a period of twenty-four hours.
examples: The sun shines during the day, and the moon shines at night.
There are seven days in a week.
Our trip to the zoo was the best day of the summer.

easy.def: The time in the morning when light first comes.
examples: We left at daybreak.
Birds sing at daybreak.
The farmer wakes at daybreak.

more.def: The time of day when light first appears in the sky.
examples: The campers woke at daybreak to watch the sun rise.
Roosters crow at daybreak on the farm.
The fishing boat left the dock before daybreak.

easy.def: A place where young children are looked after during the day.
examples: My sister goes to daycare.
The daycare is fun.
A daycare for little kids.

more.def: A place where young children are cared for during the day while their parents are at work.
examples: My little brother goes to daycare while Mom is at work.
The daycare has a playground and lots of toys.
A teacher at the daycare read a story.

easy.def: Happy thoughts you have while you are awake.
examples: I had a daydream in class.
Her daydream was about a beach.
His daydream was of flying.

more.def: A set of happy or pleasant thoughts you have while you are awake, often about things you would like to happen.
examples: I had a daydream about flying over the mountains in a hot-air balloon.
Her daydream was interrupted when the teacher called her name.
A long car ride is a good time for a daydream.

easy.def: To think happy thoughts while awake.
examples: I daydream in the car.
She daydreamed in class.
He is daydreaming.

more.def: To think happy, pleasant thoughts about things you would like to do, instead of paying attention to what is around you.
examples: I daydreamed about summer vacation while the teacher talked.
She likes to daydream on long bus rides.
He daydreamed about becoming a famous soccer player.

easy.def: The light from the sun during the day.
examples: We played until the daylight faded.
Daylight came through the window.
I woke up at daylight.

more.def: The natural light that you have during the day.
examples: We played outside until the daylight faded.
We hiked back before the daylight ran out.
The owl hides from the daylight.

easy.def: The part of the day when it is light.
examples: I play in the daytime.
The stars are not out in the daytime.
Owls sleep in the daytime.

more.def: The time of day between sunrise and sunset, when it is light.
examples: We play outside in the daytime.
Owls sleep in the daytime and hunt at night.
The daytime was warm, but the night was cold.

easy.def: Feeling confused and not able to think.
examples: I was in a daze.
The boy was in a daze.
She walked in a daze.

more.def: A state of confusion in which you cannot think clearly.
examples: I was in a daze after waking up.
The boy walked in a daze after the fall.
She stared in a daze at the huge cake.

easy.def: To shine so brightly that you cannot see, or to amaze.
examples: The sun dazzled me.
The show dazzled us.
The lights dazzle.

more.def: To shine so brightly that you cannot see well, or to amaze people with something wonderful.
examples: The bright sun dazzled my eyes.
The magician dazzled the crowd with his tricks.
The fireworks dazzled the night sky.

easy.def: So bright or beautiful that it is hard to look at.
examples: The sun is dazzling.
She wore a dazzling dress.
The lights were dazzling.

more.def: Extremely bright or beautiful, so that it amazes you.
examples: The dazzling sun made us squint.
She wore a dazzling dress covered in sequins.
The fireworks made a dazzling show in the night sky.

easy.def: In a very bright way.
examples: The sun shone dazzlingly.
The snow was dazzlingly white.
The lights flashed dazzlingly.

more.def: In a way that is so bright it is hard to look at.
examples: The snow was dazzlingly white in the sun.
The lights shone dazzlingly on the stage.
The jewel sparkled dazzlingly.
